source: RFC 0014 R1 on stored records and G5 (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-24, after the red-team review CE-9, CE-10, CE-15); RFC 0014 §5 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: A stored record CoSec reads by the reader's rule (StoredFormat) may carry crit, the members a reader must understand: an array of paths from the record's root (member names joined by '.'; through an array, each element's member), not written when empty and never written by an 8.0 writer. A reader ignores a member it does not know unless crit names it; then it refuses that one record as one a later version wrote, and never reads or rewrites it, so a member an older reader must not ignore or drop is never lost to it (RFC 0014 G5); the other records read as before. A crit that is not one (not an array, an entry that is not a path, an entry repeated, more than 16, or a member this version knows that the record does not hold) is malformed. A refused session record is answered 503 on the refresh, logout or switch that read it, the session kept; a refused record of the control plane or of a shadow window is answered 503 by the control API, without detail, never the 500 of a record that does not decode; the log tells a record a later version wrote apart from a store that is broken.
